## What Is a Principal Financial Group Internship?


A Principal Financial internship is a 10–12-week paid summer placement across one of 10 tracks at the Fortune 500 insurer and asset manager headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. Tracks span actuarial science, accounting, data and analytics, financial analytics, technology, sales, commercial real estate, investment operations, equities, and other corporate functions. All interns receive formal mentor assignments, small-group meetings with executive leadership, and professional development programming. The[actuarial track](https://careers.principal.com/internships) pairs interns with credentialed actuaries on real projects including cluster modeling, experience studies, and foreign exchange analysis, culminating in a multi-day "Actuarial code jam" team project. Named an[Ethisphere World's Most Ethical Companies 2025](https://www.principal.com/about-us) honoree, Principal pays $24–$29/hr for actuarial interns plus a $4,000 lump-sum stipend, with arranged housing, free downtown parking, and a DART bus pass included.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


Principal's eligibility requirements vary by track, with the actuarial internship carrying the most specific prerequisites:


• **Enrollment:** currently pursuing or recently completed an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited institution.


• **Actuarial exam:** the actuarial track explicitly requires at least one SOA exam completed and passed, plus a commitment to pursue FSA credentials. This is a hard filter, not a preference.


• **Coursework:** track-specific. Accounting requires 12+ hours of accounting coursework (summer) or 6+ hours (co-op). Financial Analytics requires 6+ hours of finance. CRE requires intermediate commercial real estate coursework.


• **Work authorization:** no visa sponsorship available. International students requiring sponsorship are effectively excluded.


### Does Principal Financial Have a GPA Requirement?


No. Principal does not publish a minimum GPA on any internship page or job description. The actuarial track values passed SOA exams above GPA, the accounting track values coursework hours, and the technology track values demonstrated problem-solving ability. If your GPA is below 3.0, lead with exam results, project work, or relevant technical skills rather than trying to compensate for a metric Principal does not screen on.

## What Is the Principal Financial Group Application and Interview Process Like?


Principal uses a structured interview process with behavioral-based questions. Glassdoor rates intern interview difficulty at 2.6 out of 5, making it notably approachable:


1. **Visit careers.principal.com/internships.** Browse all 10 tracks and identify the roles matching your career interests. You can apply to multiple positions.


2. **Apply online** through the Principal career site. Only applications submitted through the official site are considered. The actuarial track requires at least one passed SOA exam; the accounting track requires 12+ hours of accounting coursework.


3. **Recruiter pre-screen.** Every application is reviewed by a recruiter. If advanced, expect a traditional phone interview or an on-demand pre-recorded interview where you record answers on your own time.


4. **Assessment (some positions).** Depending on the role, you may complete an assessment on leadership, general employability, or coding. No specific platform (HackerRank, CodeSignal) is named.


5. **Behavioral interviews.** Principal uses structured interviewing with STAR-method questions. Expect one to two rounds with the hiring team. Glassdoor reviewers describe "a series of behavioral questions that tested your capacity to work collaboratively and how conflict was resolved."


6. **Decision and offer.** Expect to hear back within two weeks. Offers are contingent on background check completion. Relocation assistance is available for some positions.


Principal's own How We Hire page provides behavioral question examples: describe a time you worked under pressure, made a difficult decision, or created something new. Prepare five to six STAR stories covering these themes. Our[HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool](https://www.extern.com/post/hirevue-interview-questions-2025-free-ai-mock-tool) covers the same format.

## How Do You Stand Out at a $781 Billion Asset Manager?


Three moves, all executable before fall 2026. First, pass at least one SOA exam, because it is explicitly required for the actuarial track. Exam P (Probability) is the standard first exam. Candidates who have passed P plus one additional exam hold a meaningful advantage. Show your exam transcript proactively. Second, demonstrate genuine interest in Principal's specific business lines, not just insurance. Principal manages $781 billion in assets across retirement services, asset management, and insurance. An actuarial candidate who can speak to retirement plan design, annuity pricing, or pension risk transfer will stand out from someone who only knows auto or health insurance. Reference Principal's acquisition of Wells Fargo's retirement business to show you understand the company's strategic direction. Third, prepare STAR-format stories covering teamwork, pressure, decision-making, and creativity. Principal's How We Hire page explicitly teaches the STAR method and provides example questions. Glassdoor rates interview difficulty below average, so standard preparation puts you in strong position.

## FAQ


### Are Principal Financial internship applications open for summer 2027?


Yes, they are open now. The Actuarial Internship and Accounting Internship for summer 2027 were posted in late August 2026 at careers.principal.com. More tracks are expected to post through fall 2026. Apply immediately, as Principal fills positions on a rolling basis.


### How long is a Principal Financial internship?


Ten to twelve weeks for most tracks. Standard summer internships run approximately May through August. The Accounting track also offers a six to seven month extended co-op format, and Investment Operations runs six to nine months full-time for deeper asset class immersion.


### How much do Principal Financial interns get paid?


The actuarial internship pays $24 to $29 per hour, plus a $4,000 lump-sum stipend. The accounting internship pays $24 per hour with the same stipend. All Principal internships are paid and include arranged housing, free downtown parking, and a DART bus pass.


### Does Principal Financial sponsor visas for interns?


No. The actuarial internship job description states that visa sponsorship is not available. International students requiring work visa sponsorship are effectively excluded from the program. Permanent US work authorization is required across all tracks.


### What exams do I need for the actuarial internship?


At least one SOA actuarial exam passed. The live summer 2027 posting requires at least one actuarial exam completed and passed along with a commitment to pursue FSA credentials. Exam P (Probability) is the standard first exam most candidates complete before applying.


### Where are Principal Financial internships located?


Primarily Des Moines, Iowa, where Principal is headquartered. All confirmed summer 2027 postings are in Des Moines with hybrid or in-office options. Interns receive free downtown parking and a DART bus pass. Arranged housing is available for those relocating.


### What is the Principal Financial intern interview like?


Expect structured behavioral interviews using the STAR method. Glassdoor reviewers describe behavioral questions testing teamwork and conflict resolution. The process includes a recruiter pre-screen, possible assessment, and one to two rounds with the hiring team. Difficulty is rated 2.6 out of 5.


### Can a Principal Financial internship lead to a full-time job?


Yes, the program is designed as a talent pipeline. One Reddit user reported converting two internships into a full-time actuarial role at Principal. The company frames the internship as a pathway to full-time employment, though no exact conversion percentage is published.
